target_moa.text: Delgocitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that inhibits the activity of JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and TYK2; JAK signaling recruits STATs to cytokine receptors to induce expression of cytokine-responsive genes

citations.quote: Delgocitinib, a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, inhibits the activity of JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2).

JAK signaling involves recruitment of signal transducers and activators of transcription (STATs) to cytokine receptors, and activation and subsequent localization of STATs to the nucleus, leading to the expression of cytokine-responsive genes to induce specific biological responses in target cells.

Delgocitinib is a new molecular entity that inhibits the activity of all four Janus kinases (JAKs): JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2).

summary.text: ANZUPGO received fast track designation (June 12, 2020); breakthrough therapy and priority review requests were both denied, so the NDA underwent standard review supported by two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (DELTA 1 and DELTA 2)

citations.quote: The U.S. FDA granted fast track designation for the investigation of delgocitinib cream in the treatment of moderate to severe CHE on June 12, 2020, following a fast-track request submission on May 5, 2020.
The Applicant requested priority review designation with this NDA; however, that request was denied.

The Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness with data from two adequate and well-controlled trials, DELTA 1 and DELTA 2, that evaluated delgocitinib cream, 2% twice daily (BID) compared with vehicle for 16 weeks.
